jobs.title: HR Business Partner (m/f/x)

Working closely with managers and leadership teams, you will translate business needs and people strategies into practical HR solutions that support both employee engagement and organizational success.

Partner with and advise managers on a wide range of HR topics, including performance management, employee relations, talent development and employment legislation.

Implement and embed new and existing HR policies, procedures and organisational change initiatives.
Take ownership of designated HR topics and drive continuous improvement within your area of responsibility.

Ensure compliance with employment legislation, internal policies, quality standards and corporate guidelines.

A bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organisational Psychology or a related field.

Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively across diverse stakeholder groups.

Excellent command of both Dutch and English, written and spoken.

A competitive salary and attractive benefits package.
A collaborative and supportive working environment where respect, teamwork and continuous improvement are highly valued.

Ready to make an impact?

If you are passionate about helping people and organisations succeed, and you enjoy partnering with leaders to build high-performing teams, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and become part of Yusen Logistics.

jobs.title: People Business Partner
jobs.description:
As a People Business Partner at Sage, you work alongside the leaders who move the business forward, helping them build stronger teams, steer through change, and turn ambitious plans into results that hold up. You bring a clear point of view, a steady presence, and the kind of judgment leaders come to rely on. You tend to see what is coming before it arrives, and you are usually already thinking about what to do about it.

What you will own

Leading change that sticks. Guiding transformation, workforce planning, restructuring, and cross-functional projects with clear goals, visible sponsorship, disciplined communication, collaborator alignment, and enough structure to keep the right people moving together without slowing the work down.
Being the voice leaders rely on. Partnering with senior leaders as they set direction, offering clear guidance, candid input, and the kind of decision-focused meeting leadership that helps teams align quickly and leave with shared ownership of next steps.
Building teams that perform. Shaping talent, performance, engagement, and organizational design so people do their best work, teams pull in the same direction, and the business can grow without losing its footing.
Letting the evidence lead. Turning people metrics, patterns, and trends into choices you can defend, outcomes you can measure, and practical answers leaders can act on.
Solving the problems that do not come with a playbook. Spotting risk, gaps, and openings early, asking better questions, testing practical options, and bringing creative, sound answers before small issues grow into large ones.
Connecting the wider system. Working hand in hand with global P&C teams and Centers of Excellence while navigating complex employee relations, performance, and compliance matters toward outcomes that are fair, sound, scalable, and right for the business.

You will thrive here if

You meet leaders where they are. No two leaders are alike, and you adjust your approach to their style, context, pressure points, and readiness without losing your authenticity or lowering the bar.
You can translate without diluting. You know how to turn people strategy, policy, data, and change into language that makes sense to the leader in front of you, whether they need the headline, the risk, the options, or the next practical step.
You say what needs saying in a way it can be heard. You give leaders the straight version, even when an easier answer is sitting right there, and you know when to challenge, when to coach, and when to create space for them to get there.
You trust your own read. You are comfortable taking a position and standing behind it, and you bring original thinking instead of reaching for the default playbook.
You know the edge of what you know. When you are not certain, you say so and go find the answer, because getting it right matters more to you than appearing to have it all figured out.
You move with the business. Fast pace, shifting ground, more questions than answers? That tends to be where you do some of your best work, because you can bring enough structure, judgment, and calm to help leaders keep moving.

What you bring

Strategic Influence and Change Leadership

A track record of becoming the trusted voice behind business leaders in complex or global organizations.
Real experience guiding transformation and change, not just watching it happen around you.
A practical change-management toolkit: clear case for change, stakeholder mapping, sponsor alignment, communication cadence, manager enablement, adoption tracking, and reinforcement after launch.
The ability to shape thinking and direction at senior levels through influence rather than authority.

Business and People Expertise

Deep command of modern people practices, including organizational design, talent strategy, and workforce planning.
A history of translating business strategy into results-driven people plans.

jobs.title: Director, People Operations & Systems
jobs.description:
We are building a lean, AI-enabled People function, and the Director of People Operations & Systems will own the infrastructure that allows it to operate accurately, efficiently, and at scale. This leader is accountable for our People systems ecosystem, people data integrity, payroll governance and controls, employee lifecycle operations, and the continuous redesign of People workflows through AI, automation, and self-service.
This is a builder role. You will inherit systems and processes that need to evolve, lead our transition to a modern HR technology environment, and create an operating model that reduces manual work while strengthening accuracy, controls, and the employee and manager experience. You will be close enough to the work to understand it deeply and step in when necessary, but your primary job is to build systems, controls, talent, and workflows that do not depend on you personally executing every transaction.
You will lead core People Operations capabilities, including payroll and benefits/compliance team members, and serve as the senior operational partner to Finance, IT, Legal, Security, Talent, and People leadership. The right person combines strong HR systems and payroll judgment with a first-principles mindset: you see a clunky process and ask not only how to automate it, but whether it should exist in its current form at all.
What You Will Own

People Systems & Technology

Own the People technology ecosystem and roadmap, including HRIS architecture, system governance, integrations, access, vendor performance, and continuous improvement
Serve as the internal business owner for our planned HRIS modernization, leading requirements, data migration, configuration decisions, testing, training, rollout, and adoption in partnership with implementation experts and cross-functional stakeholders
Ensure People systems are designed around scalable workflows, clear controls, manager and employee self-service, and reliable downstream data
Partner with IT and Security on integrations, access controls, system changes, and audit requirements across the People technology stack

People Data, Analytics & Controls

Own the integrity and governance of People data, including organizational structure, job architecture fields, compensation-related data, employee records, and reporting structures
Build proactive data-quality controls that identify discrepancies before they create payroll, reporting, compliance, or employee-experience issues
Develop scalable dashboards and self-service reporting that give leaders timely insight into headcount, hiring, turnover, compensation, and talent trends
Reduce reliance on recurring manual reports by redesigning reporting workflows and automating repeatable data delivery wherever practical

Payroll Governance & Operational Risk

Lead the payroll capability and provide senior oversight of payroll operations, with accountability for accuracy, timeliness, controls, documentation, audit readiness, and effective issue resolution
Manage and develop the payroll team member responsible for day-to-day payroll execution; remain sufficiently close to the work to review controls, interrogate payroll outputs, understand multi-state requirements, and step in during high-risk or exceptional situations
Establish clear review and escalation mechanisms across People and Finance, including independent controls for high-risk payroll changes and exceptions
Redesign payroll and payroll-adjacent workflows as systems and automation mature, shifting the function toward governance, exception management, auditing, and continuous improvement rather than manual processing

Employee Lifecycle & People Operations

Own the effectiveness of the operational infrastructure supporting onboarding, offboarding, employment changes, contractor lifecycle processes, I-9/E-Verify, and Employer of Record operations for international team members
Ensure workflows are accurate, compliant, well controlled, and increasingly self-service; the role owns the effectiveness of the operating system even when another team member or system executes individual steps

jobs.title: Talent Partner - Referrals (Remote)
jobs.description:
Talent Partner - Referrals

At inspiring vet care, our people are at the heart of everything we do. As the UK’s number one vet care provider, we're trusted with the care of over 2 million animals, delivering our purpose of healthier animals and happier owners.

We’re looking for an accomplished recruiter to partner with our UK referral network, identifying and engaging exceptional veterinary professionals within one of the most specialised talent markets in the profession.

Referral recruitment requires a distinctly proactive and relationship-led approach. Success in this role will be driven by your ability to understand specialist talent markets in depth, identify and engage individuals who may not be actively considering their next career move, and build credible relationships over the longer term.

Combining headhunting, executive search principles, talent mapping and market intelligence, you’ll develop sustainable pipelines of specialist veterinary talent in multiple disciplines while partnering with senior clinical leaders to deliver both immediate and future workforce requirements.

This is a fully remote, home-based role, with travel required for meetings, veterinary congresses and industry events across the UK and Europe.

How You’ll Make a Difference

You’ll take ownership of recruitment across a portfolio of specialist referral vacancies, acting as a trusted Talent Partner to senior clinical and commercial leaders across our network.

Developing a detailed understanding of individual clinical disciplines and their respective talent markets will be central to your success. You’ll use this insight to shape recruitment strategies, advise on market conditions and provide an informed perspective on talent availability, compensation, attraction, relocation and international recruitment.

A significant focus of the role will be the proactive identification and engagement of specialist veterinary talent. Through systematic market mapping, targeted search and sustained relationship management, you’ll develop networks and pipelines that extend beyond current vacancies and strengthen our long-term ability to attract exceptional clinicians.

You’ll also:

Lead sophisticated headhunting and search strategies across specialist referral disciplines, using market mapping, professional networks and targeted sourcing to identify and engage high-calibre talent across the UK and internationally
Build and maintain meaningful long-term relationships with specialist clinicians, developing sustainable talent pipelines and communities across priority disciplines
Partner consultatively with senior clinical and hospital leaders, providing market intelligence and using evidence to influence recruitment strategy, compensation positioning, attraction approaches and realistic hiring expectations
Manage complex recruitment processes from initial engagement through to appointment, including assessment, candidate management, offer negotiation, relocation and visa sponsorship where appropriate
Represent inspiring vet care at specialist veterinary congresses, professional events and networking forums across the UK and Europe, strengthening our presence and relationships within the referral community
Use recruitment data, talent intelligence and pipeline analysis to continuously refine recruitment strategies, strengthen direct hiring capability and reduce reliance on external agencies

You Might Be a Great Fit If...

You bring significant experience of recruiting within specialist or talent-scarce markets, together with a strong track record in headhunting and/or executive search.

You are skilled at looking beyond the active candidate market: understanding where specialist talent sits, developing a comprehensive view of the market and establishing credible relationships with individuals whose career decisions may develop over an extended period.

Previous veterinary recruitment experience would be advantageous but is not essential. Of greater importance is your ability to apply sophisticated search methodology, develop specialist market expertise and operate as a credible recruitment partner to senior stakeholders.

You’ll bring:

Demonstrable expertise in headhunting, executive search, talent mapping and proactive direct sourcing within niche, specialist or difficult-to-source markets
Proven ability to identify and engage passive talent, establish credibility and develop long-term relationships through extended recruitment cycles
Strong stakeholder consulting capability, with the confidence and credibility to influence and constructively challenge senior leaders
Highly developed candidate management, assessment, negotiation and closing skills, with a focus on delivering an exceptional candidate experience
Strong commercial judgement and the ability to interpret market intelligence and recruitment data to shape effective talent strategies and prioritise activity
Excellent research, communication and relationship-building skills, combined with a proactive, resilient and highly collaborative approach
Experience within veterinary recruitment, healthcare or another specialist professional market would be advantageous, as would exposure to international recruitment, relocation and visa sponsorship.

How We’ll Support You

At inspiring vet care, we’re committed to supporting your ongoing development and wellbeing.

You’ll join an experienced Talent team and work closely with colleagues and clinical leaders who bring extensive knowledge of the veterinary profession and our referral network. We’ll support you in developing detailed knowledge of referral disciplines, specialist career pathways and the clinical communities you’ll recruit within.

You’ll have the autonomy to build and develop specialist talent networks, shape sourcing strategies and establish your own presence within the referral community, supported by opportunities to attend leading veterinary congresses and professional events across the UK and Europe.

You’ll also have the opportunity to take a genuinely long-term approach to talent acquisition. Alongside delivering against current recruitment priorities, you’ll build the relationships, market intelligence and talent pipelines that strengthen our ability to attract specialist clinicians well into the future.

What We Offer Our Team

Work-life balance
26 days annual leave (Including bank holidays)
Cycle to Work scheme
Initiatives focused on employee wellbeing
Pension
Discretionary annual bonus
Discounted staff pet care and pet insurance
Discounts and cashback across many popular retailers

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

About Amplify

Amplify helps teachers bring delight and rigor to students every day. We have become a leader in K–12 literacy, biliteracy, math, and science by building inspiring teaching and learning experiences based on research. The Amplify Classroom platform combines curriculum, assessment, and supplemental learning into one coherent high-quality instructional system. A pioneer in education since 2000, Amplify has developed deep relationships in states and districts by partnering with educators to drive implementation quality and improved outcomes. Today, Amplify serves more than 18 million students and teachers across all 50 states and on six continents. For more information, visit Amplify.com.

Job Description Summary

The Human Resources Business Partner is an individual contributor who combines hands-on execution with proactive partnership across assigned client groups. Reporting to a Senior HR Business Partner, this role serves as a trusted advisor to managers and leaders, translating business priorities and workforce needs into practical people strategies and solutions. The HRBP operates with meaningful autonomy, builds strong relationships with stakeholders, coaches managers through a broad range of people matters, and uses data and business context to identify trends, anticipate needs, and recommend action. The ideal candidate is comfortable navigating ambiguity, managing competing priorities, and knowing when to independently resolve an issue versus partnering with or escalating to the Senior HRBP, Employee Relations, Legal, or other People teams.

This role will support assigned client groups within Sales, Marketing, Product, and/or other business functions in a collaborative, matrixed, remote-first environment. The HRBP will independently own day-to-day HR partnership within a defined scope while providing visibility, recommendations, and escalation on complex or high-impact matters to the Senior HRBP.

Essential Responsibilities

Provide independent, day-to-day HR partnership to assigned managers and employees, serving as a trusted resource for practical guidance and solutions.
Build a strong understanding of assigned client groups’ business priorities, workforce needs, organizational context, and culture to anticipate issues, identify opportunities, and deliver practical, consistent guidance.
Coach managers through routine and moderately complex performance, feedback, and talent matters, including goal setting, performance documentation, corrective action, Performance Improvement Plans (PIP), talent development, and succession planning. Help managers apply expectations consistently and communicate clearly with employees.
Identify themes and trends across employee relations matters, exit feedback, engagement signals, workforce data, and other people metrics. Use data and qualitative insights to identify opportunities, develop recommendations, and communicate clear, compelling narratives to the Senior HRBPs and the broader People team to inform proactive action.
Contribute to the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of People programs, processes, policies, and manager resources. Support company and departmental diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility goals through inclusive and equitable People team practices.
Manage routine to moderately complex employee relations matters from intake through resolution, including conducting or supporting investigations, maintaining thorough and objective documentation, assessing potential risk, and recommending practical resolution options.
Advise and coordinate on timely employee lifecycle actions including job changes, promotions, transfers, reorganizations, leaves, accommodations, and terminations.
Support organizational change initiatives, including reorganizations, team changes, role changes, and other workforce transitions, in partnership with Senior HRBPs and business leaders. Help assess people impacts, identify risks and opportunities, and execute clear communication and transition plans.
Support organizational and team effectiveness initiatives by helping leaders understand workforce needs, organizational design considerations, and people-related implications of business decisions.
Support annual and recurring talent and people processes, including performance management, talent reviews, compensation planning, and promotions. Prepare managers for decision-making, promote consistency and fairness, and support effective communication of outcomes.
Guide managers in applying staffing, headcount, and compensation practices by coordinating with Compensation, Talent Acquisition, Finance, People Analytics, and other teams as needed.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Psychology, Business Administration, or a related field.
5+ years of progressive experience in Human Resources, including experience in an HR Generalist, HR Business Partner, or comparable role.
Ability to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and operate effectively in an environment with ambiguity and changing business needs.
Demonstrated willingness and courage to challenge senior leaders, push back constructively, and hold a firm stance on key people and organizational decisions.
Experience independently advising managers on employee relations, performance management, employee lifecycle processes, and conducting or supporting employee relations investigations.

Demonstrated business acumen and ability to understand how organizational goals, workforce needs, and business performance inform people decisions.
Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships and establish rapport with managers, leaders, and employees at all levels of an organization.

Significant experience in HR Operations, People Operations, or HR systems-focused roles, with ownership of regional or multi-jurisdictional operations. Prior deliverables may include (but not limited to):
Technology evaluation, re-design and implementation (ex: new HRIS system)
Significant policy design and transition (ex: you made a large scale global policy change and drove the change management)
Redesigning work flows with the use of AI/agentic solutions
Experience leading complex employee relations matters (ex: difficult policy decision, standard employee investigation)

Someone who has held an HR Business Partner role (or similar employee facing role)

Experience building or maturing contractor, consultant, or non-employee workforce processes.
Experience supporting company growth and change, with exposure to M&A, integration, or organizational transition work strongly preferred.
Ability to think beyond the current moment and design for where the company is going, not just where it is today.
Strong judgment, high discretion, and the ability to move fluidly between strategy and hands-on execution.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to turn ambiguity into clear action.
Experience in an AI-focused, high-growth, or highly innovative environment, with credible ideas for how AI and agentic approaches can level up HR Operations.

jobs.title: Recruiting Manager, Global Operations
jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

Our Global Operations Recruiting team is dedicated to building world-class talent pipelines across Airbnb's most critical operational functions. We are a collaborative, data-driven group that partners closely with business leaders across Finance, Legal, HR, Trust, Customer Experience, to attract and hire exceptional talent at scale. We set the standard for recruiting excellence and take pride in delivering an outstanding candidate experience every step of the way.

The Difference You Will Make

As Recruiting Manager, Global Operations, you will lead a team of recruiters responsible for hiring across Airbnb's global operations functions, while also personally owning and running complex, senior-level searches yourself. This is a hybrid role: part strategic people leader, part expert practitioner. You bring a consultative approach, strong people leadership instincts, and deep operational acumen, and you're equally comfortable setting strategy for your team as you are rolling up your sleeves to run a search end-to-end. You are someone who thrives in ambiguity, builds with rigor, and holds both your team and your stakeholders to a high bar. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, and you will be expected to do both well.

A Typical Day

Lead, coach, and develop a team of recruiters across global operations functions, holding a high bar for performance, candidate experience, and partnership quality.
Personally lead end-to-end searches for senior and/or executive-level roles within Global Operations, from intake through offer and close, modeling the standard you expect from your team.
Serve as a strategic talent advisor to senior business leaders across Global Operations, translating hiring needs into executable recruiting strategies.
Own team-level goals, metrics, and reporting, proactively sharing data-driven insights with stakeholders and leadership to drive accountability and continuous improvement; represent the team in recurring global forums with funnel health and hiring-progress updates.
Build and maintain strong cross-functional relationships with Finance, Employee Experience and Global Operations teams to align on headcount priorities.
Drive operational rigor across the full recruiting lifecycle, intake, sourcing strategy, pipeline management, offer execution, and closing, for both your team's requisitions and your own.
Proactively identify and resolve pipeline escalations, partnering with business leaders and cross-functional teams to address issues before they impact delivery.
Partner with Compensation, HR Business Partners, and Legal to navigate complex offer structures and ensure equitable, compliant hiring practices across global markets.
Develop scalable processes and frameworks to improve team efficiency, data integrity, and recruiter capacity planning.
Champion an exceptional, high-touch candidate experience, with particular attention to senior-level candidates, ensuring consistent and timely communication at every stage of the hiring process.
Exceptional data fluency with the ability to build, interpret, and present recruiting dashboards and pipeline analytics from the ground up; you do not wait for data to come to you, you architect the infrastructure, identify the gaps, and translate complex metrics into clear narratives that drive stakeholder alignment and inform hiring strategy at the leadership level
Establish yourself as a subject-matter expert and trusted voice in operations recruiting, both internally and in the broader talent market.
Contribute to cross-functional recruiting initiatives, including process design, tooling decisions, and recruiter development programs.
Represent the recruiting team in executive-level conversations, including capacity planning, headcount reviews, and quarterly business updates.

Your Expertise

9+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including a demonstrated track record personally leading senior-level searches, and at least 2 years managing and developing a team of recruiters.
Deep functional expertise in at least one Global Operations sub-function is highly preferred (e.g., Customer Support, Trust & Safety), not just general familiarity with operations hiring.
Demonstrated success recruiting for global operations, business functions, or non-technical roles at a technology company.
Proven ability to build trust and credibility with senior business leaders and act as a genuine strategic partner rather than a transactional hiring resource.
Experience conducting market research, talent mapping, and proactive pipeline-building for senior-level roles, not solely reactive, requisition-driven sourcing.
Strong data orientation with the ability to interpret pipeline metrics, forecast capacity needs, and translate insights into action.
Experience navigating complex, multi-stakeholder hiring environments across multiple geographies and business units.
Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with sound judgment in ambiguous situations.
Proficiency with enterprise recruiting and HRIS tools such as Greenhouse, Workday, Gem or comparable systems.
A track record of building inclusive pipelines and championing diversity throughout the hiring process.
Genuine comfort carrying a personal search load alongside people leadership, this role requires the ability to lead strategically and operate hands-on, at a senior individual-contributor level, when the work demands it.

Due to the nature of this position, the successful applicant will need to be based in California or PST time zone

We’re looking for someone who can become deeply embedded in the EPM ecosystem, build relationships across the OneStream, Oracle EPM, Pigment, and broader performance management communities, and develop the networks that help us find exceptional talent before we need it.

EPM practice leadership responsible for growing our OneStream, Oracle EPM, Pigment, and broader performance management capabilities.

Go-to-market and business development leaders helping expand Thought Logic’s presence within the EPM ecosystem.

A builder’s mentality. You’re energized by creating networks, processes, strategies, and relationships rather than simply inheriting them.

Own talent acquisition for a highly strategic and growing part of our business.

Spanish and English bilingual required

Company Overview

Gold Leaf is a farming company whose core focus is to build farms, family, and a future we're proud of. We own and operate ~12,000 acres of almonds, pistachios, and dates in California and Arizona, making us a top ~15 grower of these crops globally.
Our North Star is to leave the world better than we found it. We invest in our team so that we can invest in differentiated, sustainable farming — and drive exceptional financial results. Our farm workers have a $23 starting wage in California, fully paid healthcare, retirement, and parental leave. Our farms use technology and research-based strategies to maximize production while minimizing use of precious natural resources.

Role Overview

The People Operations Manager is a core owner of Gold Leaf’s People function, responsible for managing day-to-day people processes with accuracy and care. The role partners directly with managers across the full employee lifecycle and improves the systems and structures that allow GLF to attract, develop, and retain the Right People in the Right Seats. Core responsibilities of the People Operations Manager include:

Centralized People Operations (75% of time)

The People Operations Manager owns the execution, improvement, and communication of GLF's centralized people processes, serving as a trusted, day-to-day point of contact for all employees. This role challenges the status quo to continuously refine people processes, strengthen cultural alignment, and enhance employee experience.
Own execution of centralized processes: hiring, onboarding, payroll, benefits, performance management, safety, employee experience, and HR compliance
Identify process gaps and implement low-bureaucracy improvements through automation, elimination, or outsourcing
Build self-service resources that let employees navigate the People function independently
Serve as a responsive, knowledgeable resource for employees, providing clear support and building their confidence navigating the employee experience at GLF
Own Rippling as the single source of truth for people data, ensuring accuracy and building automations that reduce manual work
Partner with internal teams to ensure they have the access and information they need from People systems to do their jobs
Support the co-employment complexity of GLF's FLC model, including seasonal transitions and I-9 compliance at scale, so hourly farm workers experience Gold Leaf's culture even through contractor relationships

HR Business Partner (25% of time)

The People Operations Manager partners directly with managers as a hands-on people expert, providing credible, culturally grounded guidance across the employee lifecycle.
Own the RPRS (Right Person Right Seat) process end to end, coaching managers through evaluation conversations that drive real personnel decisions
Partner with managers on hiring, onboarding, performance management, and employee relations with sound judgment and low bureaucracy
Provide guidance that reflects GLF's culture and operating principles, equipping managers with the tools, frameworks, and knowledge to handle people situations with greater confidence over time
Contribute to GLF's talent strategy by identifying patterns, gaps, and opportunities surfaced through day-to-day people operations
Partner with the VP of Operations on culture programming: quarterly gatherings, recognition programs, and the structures that make Gold Leaf's culture durable across a decentralized team
Support the delivery of a differentiated, best-in-class employee experience rooted in GLF's culture, operating principles, and long-term vision

Suggested Skills And Experience

Working knowledge of California employment law and multi-state HR compliance
Tech-savvy, with a natural inclination to automate and streamline manual work; Rippling or similar HRIS experience a plus
Strong process instincts, with a bias toward simplicity over complexity or added headcount
Experience in agriculture or other operationally intensive industries strongly preferred; familiarity with FLC models or seasonal workforce management a plus
Ability and willingness to travel to our California and Arizona farms on a routine basis

Acts Like an Owner: Thinks and acts with a sense of accountability and investment in GLF's long-term success. Shares responsibility when things go wrong and shares credit when we win.

Puts Family First: Genuinely cares about the people of GLF and creates an environment where great people want to work and grow.

Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We're hiring a People Operations Manager to own our People data and the reporting built on top of it, alongside a slice of the operational work that generates it.

Cohere is scaling fast and leadership needs numbers they can trust. Today those numbers take too long to produce and they don't always agree with each other. Reporting is only as good as the data underneath it, which is why this role runs real processes as well as reporting on them.

This is a hands-on building role. You will own headcount, attrition and cost reporting, define what our metrics actually mean, and own benefits administration and employee records end to end. You will own the answer, not just the spreadsheet. A useful lens; this role means nobody has to debate whose number is right.

You'll join a small HR Operations team during our Rippling implementation, which means greenfield opportunity and real influence over how our data is structured for the next few years.

What You'll Do

Own the numbers

Own headcount, attrition and people cost reporting end to end
Build the exec and board level reporting our leadership relies on
Define what our metrics mean, rather than producing whatever is asked for

Fix the data underneath

Reconcile People and Finance headcount, and keep them reconciled
Clean up the taxonomies that make reporting unreliable, starting with termination reasons
Chase the data quality problems nobody has asked you to chase
Build the checks that stop bad data entering in the first place

Own the data model

Own our employee data model, definitions and governance
Work with the HRIS team so the system supports the reporting we need
Push and challenge current systems to meet your data vision

Own Benefits Administration And Records

Own US and global benefits administration, renewal cycles and open enrolment
Own employee records, employment verification and data requests
Support the front line team who handle day to day employee questions

Make reporting self-serve

Automate the recurring reporting so it produces itself
Give managers and leaders access to their own numbers
Reduce the number of requests that need a person at all

Build For What's Coming

Produce reporting that stands up to audit and external diligence
Work with Finance and IT on the controls and evidence our data needs to carry
Design for a company several times our current size

Manage a team

Led and developed a high-performing team through regular coaching, feedback, and performance management while maintaining team cohesion and morale
Managed day-to-day operations and resource allocation for a small team, balancing project priorities, resolving conflicts, and ensuring timely delivery of deliverables within budget constraints

You may be a good fit if you

5+ years of people analytics and reporting experience, within fast-paced, scaling environments
Meaningful experience delivering people operations solutions across all aspects of the talent journey
Experienced in HRIS implementation or migration
Experience building reports from scratch
Proactively identify and resolve data quality issues, maintaining high standards for clean, reliable analytics data
Effectively communicate data insights by explaining numerical findings, their source methodology, and rationale for discrepancies with alternative interpretations
Write clearly and document by default
Have run operations across multiple countries and entities, including EOR or contractor populations
Are comfortable anywhere across the employee journey, from hire to exit
Pick up new tools quickly and become the person others ask
Enjoy building elegant solutions to messy operational problems

Bonus if you have

Worked in Rippling, or implemented it
People management experience
Built reporting in a BI tool, or worked comfortably in SQL
Been in a company through IPO readiness or SOC 2 and SOX preparation

What we're not looking for

Someone who waits for a report request and fills it. This role decides what we measure and makes the underlying data good enough to trust. If you would rather be handed a spec than write one, this is not the role for you.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

For real change to happen, everyone needs a clear path to positive impact. That’s why Textile Exchange believes that approachable, step-by-step instruction paired with collective action can change the system to make preferred materials and fibers an accessible default, mobilizing leaders through attainable strategies, proven solutions, and a driven community.

At Textile Exchange, materials matter. To learn more, visit TextileExchange.org.

Working at Textile Exchange

We work remotely with a team located in 20+ countries. We work collaboratively on important environmental issues around the world by working and interacting with farming groups, processors, brands, retailers, and environmental experts in the textile and fashion industries around the world. We offer an opportunity to join a cutting-edge global environmental nonprofit and to help strengthen the impact of our organization.

Position Summary

The People Operations Lead is a member of the Leadership Team and serves as primary strategic support to the Senior Director, People & Culture — translating direction into workable plans and representing the Senior Director's priorities to the organization when needed. jobs.title: HR Generalist & Talent Acquisition Specialist
jobs.description:
About Spotlight Media

Spotlight Media is a leading TikTok Shop Partner agency, scaling some of the most recognizable brands in the new age of social commerce. Unlike traditional agencies, we don’t believe in cookie-cutter playbooks—every strategy we craft is custom-built to unlock our clients’ full potential on TikTok Shop. As a TikTok Shop–only agency, our entire focus, from the initiatives we pursue to the talent we hire, is singularly dedicated to driving growth on the platform.

We’ve guided brands through the full funnel- from launch to scaling into the millions in GMV-and we’re just getting started.

We believe the future of e-commerce is social. That’s why we’re building a team of high-agency individuals who thrive on ownership, autonomy, and speed. Spotlight is not just a place to execute campaigns—it’s a blank canvas where ambitious people can build real leverage, take on increasing responsibility, and grow into senior operators quickly. Our culture is high-performing, entrepreneurial, and unapologetically ambitious.

Join us, and you’ll have the trust, resources, and runway to redefine what’s possible for the world’s leading brands.

The Role

The HR Generalist & Talent Acquisition Specialist will serve as Spotlight Media's primary recruiter and HR point person.

The ideal candidate is someone who genuinely enjoys recruiting and interviewing, knows how to identify strong candidates, and can quickly understand what makes someone a good fit for a particular role.

You will be responsible for managing the recruiting process from sourcing through initial interviews while also overseeing the company's day-to-day HR administration, including onboarding, offboarding, payroll coordination, time-off tracking, employee documentation, and employee relations.

This person will interact with candidates, employees, managers, and leadership on a regular basis, so excellent verbal and written communication skills are essential.

Key Responsibilities

Talent Acquisition & Recruiting — Primary Responsibility

Own Spotlight Media's recruiting process from job opening through candidate handoff/hire.
Develop and execute proactive recruiting strategies to identify qualified candidates.
Conduct outbound recruiting through LinkedIn, email, direct messaging, job boards, professional networks, and other channels.
Source candidates for a variety of positions across the organization.
Review resumes and applications and determine which candidates meet the requirements of each role.
Conduct initial screening calls and first-round interviews.
Develop thoughtful interview questions and evaluation criteria for different positions.
Assess candidates based on qualifications, communication skills, experience, cultural/team fit, and potential for success in the role.
Provide clear and objective candidate feedback to hiring managers and leadership.
Coordinate interviews between candidates and hiring managers.
Maintain an organized candidate pipeline and recruiting database/ATS.
Follow up with candidates throughout the recruiting process and provide a professional candidate experience.
Help develop and continuously improve Spotlight Media's recruiting process.
Track recruiting metrics such as applicants, interviews, candidates sourced, time-to-hire, and hiring conversion rates.
Build and maintain a pipeline of potential candidates for frequently hired positions.
Help write and optimize job descriptions and job postings for LinkedIn, Indeed, and other recruiting platforms.

HR Administration

Manage the employee onboarding process for new hires.
Ensure new employees complete required documentation and onboarding requirements.
Coordinate equipment, systems access, accounts, and other onboarding needs.
Manage employee offboarding and ensure a smooth transition when employees leave the company.
Coordinate the return of company property and removal of access to company systems.
Maintain accurate and organized employee records.
Track vacation, sick time, and other employee time-off.
Maintain company HR policies and documentation.
Assist with payroll processing and ensure payroll information is accurate and submitted on time.
Coordinate with payroll providers and/or internal leadership regarding payroll issues.
Maintain accurate employee information and compensation records.
Help ensure HR processes are consistently followed across the organization.

Employee Relations & Management Support

Serve as a trusted point of contact for employees regarding HR-related questions and concerns.
Partner with managers and leadership on employee performance and workplace issues.
Help managers navigate employee performance concerns and disciplinary situations.
Participate in employee termination processes when warranted.
Conduct termination/offboarding meetings when appropriate and ensure the process is handled professionally and respectfully.
Maintain appropriate confidentiality when dealing with sensitive employee information.
Help leadership identify and address employee-related issues before they become larger problems.

Required Qualifications

What We're Looking For

3+ years of professional HR and/or recruiting experience.
Significant hands-on recruiting experience, particularly with outbound candidate sourcing.
Demonstrated experience conducting phone/video screening interviews and first-round interviews.
Experience recruiting for multiple types of roles, rather than specializing in only one position or industry.
Strong understanding of the full recruiting lifecycle.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Extremely articulate and comfortable communicating with candidates and employees.
Strong interviewing and candidate-evaluation skills.
Highly organized and able to manage multiple open positions and HR responsibilities simultaneously.
Strong attention to detail.
Comfortable handling confidential and sensitive employee information.
Experience with HRIS, ATS, Ashby, payroll, recruiting, or other HR technology platforms.
Strong proficiency with Google Workspace and common business software.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a fast-growing company or startup environment.
Experience recruiting for remote or distributed teams.
Experience recruiting for sales, marketing, account management, operations, or other professional positions.
Experience in digital marketing, e-commerce, creator economy, social media, or TikTok Shop.
Experience developing recruiting processes from the ground up.
Experience working with employees across multiple geographic locations.
Experience with payroll administration and employee benefits administration.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is first and foremost a great recruiter and interviewer
.

You should be someone who can look at a job description, understand what success in the position looks like, identify where strong candidates are likely to be found, reach out to them, and determine during an initial conversation whether they are worth moving forward.

You should also be comfortable switching gears. One day you may be sourcing candidates for an Account Manager; the next you may be onboarding a new employee, helping a manager address a performance issue, processing payroll information, or conducting an employee offboarding.

We Are Looking For Someone Who

Is confident and highly articulate.
Can build rapport quickly with candidates.
Knows how to ask good questions and, more importantly, listen to the answers.
Can distinguish between someone who interviews well and someone who is actually qualified.
Is comfortable conducting difficult conversations when necessary.
Takes ownership rather than waiting to be told what to do.
Is highly organized and follows through.
Can handle confidential information with discretion.
Is comfortable working in a fast-paced, growing company.
Is comfortable recruiting for positions they may not have personally held.
Has excellent judgment when evaluating people.
Is professional but approachable.
Can balance the needs of employees, managers, and the company.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role will primarily be measured by the quality and effectiveness of our recruiting process.

Within This Role, You Will Be Expected To

Consistently build strong candidate pipelines for our open positions.
Generate qualified candidates through proactive outbound recruiting.
Conduct high-quality screening and first-round interviews.
Help hiring managers spend their time interviewing only the most promising candidates.
Improve our overall time-to-hire without sacrificing candidate quality.
Create a professional and positive candidate experience.
Keep our HR processes organized, accurate, and compliant.
Ensure employees have a smooth experience when joining and leaving Spotlight Media.
Provide leadership with reliable HR information and support.
Become a trusted resource for both employees and management.

Why Join Spotlight Media?

Spotlight Media is a growing company operating in one of the most rapidly evolving areas of digital commerce.

This is an opportunity to join at a stage where you can have a meaningful impact on how the company builds its team and develops its HR infrastructure
.

You will have significant ownership over recruiting and the opportunity to help build the processes, systems, and standards that will support Spotlight Media as we continue to grow.

If you are an experienced recruiter who also has strong HR generalist capabilities—and you enjoy building teams, interviewing people, and helping a growing company hire great talent—we would love to hear from you.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive salary based on experience
Medical, Dental and Vision
401K
Take it as you need it PTO after 90 days.
Remote work environment
This role reports to the GM of Spotlight Media
Opportunity for professional growth within a rapidly growing company

Spotlight Media is an equal opportunity employer.

Compensation Range: $50K - $65.5K

Deep expertise hiring across the full GTM org — AEs, SDRs, sales leaders, marketers, and CS — with a strong understanding of what top-performing revenue talent looks like.
Hands-on experience using modern AI and digital tools for sourcing, screening, outreach, and candidate engagement, with a track record of building AI-driven workflows into the recruiting process.
Excellent stakeholder and relationship management skills, with demonstrated ability to partner with and influence executive leadership.

jobs.title: Global Talent Acquisition Specialist
jobs.description:
Overview

Asiacruit BPO is seeking a dedicated and proactive Global Talent Acquisition Specialist to join our People team. This role is responsible for managing end-to-end recruitment activities across multiple regions, building strong talent pipelines, partnering with hiring managers, and delivering a positive candidate experience that supports the company’s global growth objectives. The ideal candidate combines hands-on sourcing and selection expertise with strong stakeholder management, cultural awareness, and a data-informed approach to hiring.

Essential Responsibilities

Owner of full-cycle recruitment: Manage requisition intake, job posting, candidate sourcing, screening, coordinating interviews, offer management, and onboarding handoffs for roles across functions and geographies.
Strategic sourcing: Proactively build and maintain diverse talent pipelines using direct sourcing, job boards, social media, referrals, and partnerships with universities and agencies.
Stakeholder partnership: Collaborate closely with hiring managers and HR business partners to define role requirements, hiring timelines, and selection criteria; provide market insights and recruiting strategy recommendations.
Candidate experience: Ensure timely, respectful, and consistent communication with candidates throughout the process; represent the employer brand positively at every touchpoint.
Assessment and selection: Conduct structured interviews, competency assessments, and reference checks; ensure selection decisions align with company values and hiring best practices.
Hiring operations: Maintain accurate candidate and requisition data in the applicant tracking system (ATS); manage offer approvals, background checks, and onboarding documentation.
Diversity, equity, and inclusion: Drive inclusive sourcing practices and support initiatives to increase diverse representation across the workforce.
Recruiting metrics and continuous improvement: Track KPIs such as time-to-fill, quality of hire, and sourcing channel effectiveness; analyze data and recommend process improvements.
Employer branding & recruitment marketing: Support local and global employer branding efforts, attend recruitment events, and develop content to attract top talent.
Compliance and confidentiality: Ensure recruitment practices comply with local employment laws and internal policies; handle confidential information with discretion.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Psychology, or a related field preferred.
3+ years of full-cycle recruitment experience, ideally with exposure to international or multi-region hiring.
Experience using an applicant tracking system (ATS) and recruitment tools; comfortable maintaining accurate data and producing recruitment reports.
Strong sourcer skills with proven ability to find and engage passive candidates across channels.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and negotiation skills; able to build credibility with stakeholders at all levels.
Cultural sensitivity and experience working with diverse teams across time zones.
Analytical mindset with experience tracking recruiting metrics and using data to drive decisions.
High level of organization, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple requisitions simultaneously.
Familiarity with local employment laws and hiring compliance in multiple jurisdictions preferred.
Willingness to work flexible hours occasionally to accommodate different time zones.

Why Build Your Career With Us?

Competitive compensation and benefits, including health coverage and performance-based rewards.
Opportunities for professional growth through training programs and a supportive learning culture.
Collaborative global team and a chance to shape hiring strategies across markets.
A commitment to work-life balance with flexible work arrangements where applicable.

Application Instructions

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and why you are interested in this role. Qualified applicants will be contacted for the next steps in our recruitment process.

jobs.description:
For over four decades, PAR Technology Corporation (NYSE: PAR) has been a leader in restaurant technology, empowering brands worldwide to create lasting connections with their guests. Our innovative solutions and commitment to excellence provide comprehensive software and hardware that enable seamless experiences and drive growth for over 100,000 restaurants in more than 110 countries. Embracing our "Better Together" ethos, we offer Unified Customer Experience solutions, combining point-of-sale, digital ordering, loyalty and back-office software solutions as well as industry-leading hardware and drive-thru offerings. To learn more, visit partech.com or connect with us on LinkedIn, X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, and Instagram.

Position Description

We are seeking a Senior Manager, NA Talent Acquisition, to lead our North America recruiting team and serve as a trusted talent advisor to business leaders and hiring managers across the organization. This role is responsible for translating workforce needs into thoughtful staffing strategies, aligning recruiting resources to business priorities, and driving hiring outcomes across technical, go-to-market, and corporate functions. The successful candidate will bring strong people leadership, recruiting expertise, and operational discipline, with the ability to coach hiring managers through complex hiring decisions, leverage data and insights to improve outcomes, and balance speed, quality, and candidate experience while leading a high-performing recruiting team.

Position Location:
US – Remote (Eastern or Central time zone)

Reports To:
Head of Global Talent Strategy

What We’re Looking For

8+ years of progressive talent acquisition experience, including leadership of recruiting teams in fast-paced, growing organizations
Proven track record hiring across technical, GTM, and corporate/business functions simultaneously
Experience managing a distributed/remote recruiting team
Strong command of TA metrics (time-to-fill, offer acceptance, quality of hire) and how to use them to drive decisions
Hands-on experience with modern ATS platforms (Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, or similar) and a track record of driving adoption of new tools or systems
Experience partnering with senior leaders and hiring managers on workforce planning, staffing strategy, and hiring prioritization
Strong ability to influence and hold hiring managers accountable throughout the hiring process
Comfort operating in ambiguity

Additional Skills

Experience using AI, automation, and recruiting technology to improve efficiency and hiring outcomes
Strong ability to influence hiring leaders and drive accountability throughout the hiring process
Experience using recruiting metrics and market insights to inform workforce planning and talent decisions
Demonstrated success leading, coaching, and developing recruiting teams
Strong commitment to candidate experience, structured hiring, and continuous improvement

Unleash your potential: What you will be doing and owning:

Lead and develop a high-performing remote recruiting team by setting priorities, coaching team members, removing obstacles, and ensuring consistent delivery against hiring goals
Own hiring outcomes end-to-end: deliver hundreds of hires per year across diverse functions and levels while improving time-to-fill and pipeline quality in parallel
Drive candidate experience and conversion: maintain a best-in-class offer acceptance rate through strong candidate experience and close partnership with hiring teams
Partner with business leaders and hiring managers to develop thoughtful staffing plans, prioritize hiring needs, assess talent market realities, and align recruiting efforts to business objectives.
Build strong partnerships with hiring managers by setting clear expectations, driving hiring discipline, and ensuring effective decision-making throughout the recruiting process.
Implement structured hiring practices: roll out and continuously improve intake processes, calibrated interview loops, and scorecards that raise hiring manager satisfaction and hiring quality
Optimize recruiting technology, processes, and reporting to improve team productivity, hiring manager experience, and decision-making
Elevate employer brand: own the careers site and job description strategy to improve applicant quality and grow employee referrals
Leverage recruiting metrics and market insights to identify opportunities, improve hiring outcomes, and provide data-driven recommendations to business leaders
Manage vendor, agency strategy and RPO: optimize agency partnerships and vendor spend to stay below market cost benchmarks without sacrificing quality
Evaluate and implement technology, automation, and AI-enabled tools that improve recruiter efficiency, hiring manager experience, and candidate engagement

Interview Process

Interview #1: Phone Screen with Talent Acquisition Team

Interview #2: Video interview with the Hiring Manager (via MS Teams)

Interview #3: Video interview with the Team (via MS Teams)

jobs.description:
Knix is an award-winning intimate apparel and activewear brand that is re-inventing intimates for real life. Through our innovative products and our engaged community, we are empowering people everywhere to be unapologetically free. Launched in 2013, we are one of the fastest-growing intimate apparel brands in North America and are globally recognized as an innovator within the apparel space. We reach over 3 million customers through our online stores, Knix retail locations across North America and channels such as wholesale and Amazon. We are revolutionizing the apparel industry with our best-in-class customer experience, innovative products and brands Knix, Kt by Knix, and Mntd. Come join us if you are looking for a purpose-driven and authentic career!

We’re looking for an Associate HR Business Partner who will support Western Canada and is energized by supporting high-performing, people-first retail teams. In this role, you will work closely with District Managers, store leaders and hourly team members to support day-to-day HR needs while helping scale initiatives that keep pace with a fast-moving retail environment.

You will support the full employee lifecycle across our stores by delivering HR programs, coaching leaders, addressing employee concerns, supporting onboarding and development, and ensuring a consistent and positive experience for our retail teams. Key focus areas include performance and coaching, employee relations, staffing and workforce planning, HR program deployment, retail compliance and employee engagement.

As a core member of the People Team, you will partner with Retail Operations, People Operations, and Talent Acquisition to drive business goals while ensuring our retail employees feel supported, empowered, and set up for success every day.

About You:

You are a hands-on, approachable HR professional with a people-first mindset and a passion for supporting hourly retail employees and leaders.
You build trust quickly and collaborate effectively with store leaders, retail associates, and cross-functional teams.
You thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment and can shift priorities based on business needs.
You enjoy working on the ground—with stores, with leaders, and with associates—to understand challenges and create practical, scalable solutions.
You are proactive and resourceful, with strong coaching and listening skills that help leaders develop their teams and navigate employee situations confidently.
You are excited about building repeatable processes, tools, and resources as our retail network expands.
You bring strong judgment, discretion, and a collaborative approach to problem solving.

The Opportunity:

Serve as the primary People partner for assigned retail stores, building trusted relationships with District Managers, store leaders, and team members.
Coach and support retail leaders across performance management, delivering feedback, communication skills, employee development, team dynamics, and day to day people decisions.
Support employee relations matters including conflict resolution, policy interpretation, performance concerns, and workplace issues, escalating more complex or higher risk matters when appropriate.
Support investigations and maintain clear and appropriate documentation.
Help ensure employment practices across assigned stores comply with applicable legislation and align with Knix policies and practices.

jobs.title: People Operations Lead
jobs.description:
About Edra

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.

The Role

Edra is 30+ people across New York and London, with aggressive hiring plans in both offices. Every one of those people runs through an offer, payroll in one of two countries, equity in one of two tax regimes, benefits, and the compliance layer underneath it all. We've laid the foundation; now we want someone to own it, and to build the version that gets us to 60, 100, and beyond.

You'll own the employee lifecycle end to end in both countries: US and UK payroll, benefits in both regimes, onboarding, and people compliance across two jurisdictions. At most companies, people ops is carved into slices; here you own the whole stack, with real autonomy to determine how it runs. You'll own these systems internally, working directly with our payroll providers, benefits brokers, accountants, and employment counsel where specialist expertise is needed.

That's the exciting part, so we'll be specific about it: this is a builder and operator role. You'll inherit working processes and be expected to replace each one as we outgrow it: automating what's manual, rebuilding for scale, and designing the systems a much larger Edra will still be running down the line. And because we're an AI company, we expect you to build like one. Edra's platform is available to you as a tool for your own function, and we want you using it (along with everything else in a modern AI startup stack) to build and run a people operation that's leaner, faster, and more precise than a traditional people operation. If you've ever looked at a payroll reconciliation or an onboarding checklist and thought “a system should be doing this!” this is the place to prove it.

One thing to be upfront about: comp philosophy, equity strategy, and performance management remain Founder-owned. You'll make those programs operationally excellent: the data, tooling, process, communication, and execution behind them.

What You'll Do

Be the first point of contact for operational people questions (payroll, benefits, leave, equity administration, and employment logistics) and resolve them quickly and clearly.
Own US and UK payroll end to end: run it, reconcile it, handle joiners and leavers, catch problems before they reach a paycheck, and fix the ones that do fast.
Design and build our onboarding program from first principles, so new hires are set up to take ownership and have impact from day one, in either office.
Automate onboarding and offboarding processes across both entities: equipment and access provisioning, benefits enrollment, compliance training, and more.
Administer benefits in both countries: US healthcare and 401(k), including open enrollment and renewals; UK pension and benefits.
Own the operational compliance calendar across both countries, including required payroll, benefits, employment, and personnel processes and filings.
Keep Rippling accurate as the source of record for headcount, comp, and org data, and extend it wherever it can take work off a human
Build automations and internal tooling for repetitive people workflows, using Edra’s own platform and other AI tools wherever they can improve speed, accuracy, or employee experience.

What We’re Looking For

You've owned significant parts of people operations at a startup through a growth phase. You've personally processed payroll, fixed benefits enrollment errors, and onboarded new team members, not just managed vendors who did.
You've worked across US and UK employment infrastructure, or have international people ops experience and can close the gap quickly.
You default to systems. When something breaks twice, you fix the process, and when a task is repetitive, you automate it rather than staffing it.
You're curious about what AI tooling can do for an operations function, and you'd rather experiment and find out than wait for a vendor to tell you.
You're detail-oriented at the level this work requires. Errors in payroll and benefits are visible to everyone—you make sure they don’t happen.
You write clearly, especially when explaining equity, benefits, and policy to people who aren't specialists.
You handle confidential comp and performance information with discretion.

Bonus Points

UK payroll and pensions depth
Experience standing up new benefits programs in the US and UK
Fluency with Rippling
Track record of building automation or tooling inside an ops function

Watch our Series A announcement video
Read our blog post from our launch
Learn more about what we're building

Competitive base salary & meaningful equity

Top plans with 100% premium coverage in the US (and a One Medical membership)

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.

The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.

What We Value

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

Seek Excellence.
Be Selective To Be Effective.
Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
Disagree Transparently.
Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
Build Dream Teams.

Who You Are

Galaxy is seeking a People Operations Manager, Global Payroll & HRIS to join our People team in a hands-on, execution-focused role supporting our global workforce. This position will initially join on a temporary-to-permanent basis and will play a critical role in two key areas: global payroll operations and the implementation of Workday, with a targeted go-live date of January 1, 2027. In your first three-six months, success will mean helping Galaxy deliver a clean and well-controlled Workday go-live, ensuring payroll readiness and data integrity, and establishing scalable processes that can transition into steady-state People Operations

Leading up to go-live, this individual will partner closely with People, Payroll, Finance, Technology, external implementation partners, and other key stakeholders to support the successful implementation of Workday. This will include data validation and migration, business process design, testing, integrations, payroll readiness, documentation, and change management.

At the same time, this person will help manage and strengthen Galaxy's global payroll operations, ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time and that payroll processes, controls, data, and vendor relationships can scale with the organization.

Following implementation, the role will transition toward ongoing ownership and optimization of Workday and global payroll operations, including system administration, data integrity, reporting, process improvement, controls, and the employee experience.

We're looking for someone who enjoys being close to the details while understanding the broader operational picture - someone who can identify an issue in a payroll reconciliation or employee record, work cross-functionally to resolve it, and then improve the underlying process so it doesn't happen again.

What You’ll Do

Workday Implementation & HRIS
Serve as a key People Operations partner for Galaxy's Workday implementation ahead of the January 1, 2027 go-live.
Partner with internal stakeholders and external implementation resources to support requirements gathering, business process design, system configuration, integrations, and implementation activities.
Coordinate and execute data preparation, cleansing, validation, and migration activities to ensure accurate employee and payroll data within Workday
Develop and execute user acceptance testing (UAT), document results, identify issues, and partner with appropriate stakeholders through resolution.
Support payroll parallel testing and other payroll-readiness activities ahead of go-live.
Help establish scalable HRIS processes, controls, documentation, and governance.
Develop process documentation, SOPs, training materials, and resources for People team members, managers, and employees.
Support change management, training, and communications associated with the Workday launch.
Following go-live, help manage ongoing Workday administration, including business processes, employee data, reporting, security/access, system updates, and issue resolution.
Continuously identify opportunities to improve, automate, and scale People processes through Workday and other technologies.

Global Payroll
Support the end-to-end administration of payroll across Galaxy's global employee population, partnering with internal teams and third-party payroll providers as appropriate.
Review payroll inputs and outputs to ensure employees are paid accurately, completely, and on time.
Perform payroll audits, reconciliations, and variance analyses and proactively investigate and resolve discrepancies.
Coordinate employee lifecycle changes impacting payroll, including new hires, terminations, compensation changes, bonuses, benefits deductions, leaves, and other employee changes.
Partner with Finance on payroll funding, reconciliations, reporting, and related accounting requirements.
Work with People team partners to ensure HRIS, payroll, benefits, and employee data remain aligned across systems and vendors.
Support payroll compliance requirements across applicable jurisdictions and partner with internal and external subject-matter experts as needed.
Manage day-to-day relationships with payroll vendors, escalating and resolving issues while holding partners accountable for service and accuracy.
Maintain payroll calendars, controls, documentation, and standard operating procedures.
Identify opportunities to standardize and strengthen global payroll processes as Galaxy continues to grow.

People Operations
Maintain a high standard of employee data accuracy and integrity across People systems.
Produce and analyze People and payroll data to identify trends, discrepancies, and opportunities for operational improvement.
Support employee inquiries related to payroll, HR systems, and People processes, providing a high level of service and discretion.
Partner cross-functionally across People, Finance, Legal, Technology, and other teams on projects affecting employee data and operations.
Support audits, compliance requests, reporting, and other People Operations initiatives as needed.
Handle highly sensitive and confidential employee information with sound judgment and discretion.
Support global payroll operations across multiple jurisdictions (e.g., US, UK, Ireland, Portugal, and EOR-supported countries), including timesheet approvals, payroll data prep, and coordination with in-country payroll vendors.
Assist with new hire onboarding, employee data changes, transfers, and offboarding processes within Workday and related HR systems.
Prepare reports, reconciliations, and ad hoc analyses to support payroll and people operations initiatives.
Help document processes and maintain SOPs for HRIS, payroll, and people operations workflows.
Respond to employee and manager inquiries related to payroll, HR data, and system access with a high level of accuracy and discretion.

What We’re Looking For

6+ years of relevant experience in People Operations, payroll, HRIS, HR technology, or a related field.
Hands-on experience supporting payroll operations; global or multi-country payroll experience strongly preferred.
Experience working with Workday or another enterprise HRIS; direct Workday implementation experience is strongly preferred.
Experience participating in an HRIS implementation, migration, configuration, or significant system transformation is highly desirable.
Strong understanding of the connection between HRIS data, payroll, benefits, Finance, and employee lifecycle processes.
Demonstrated ability to reconcile complex datasets, identify discrepancies, and drive issues through resolution.
Strong Excel skills and comfort working with large datasets, reporting, and analysis.
Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple time-sensitive workstreams simultaneously.
Strong project management skills and the ability to keep deliverables moving across multiple stakeholders.
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment where processes may still be evolving.
Takes ownership, works effectively both independently and collaboratively, and knows when to escalate issues.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical or operational issues for different audiences.
Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive employee and compensation information.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant professional experience.

Bonus Points

Experience with a Workday HCM and/or Payroll implementation, particularly involving a January 1 or year-start cutover.
Experience supporting payroll across North America, EMEA, and/or APAC.
Experience working with multiple local payroll providers or a global payroll platform.
Familiarity with payroll integrations, data feeds, benefits integrations, and Finance/GL processes.
Experience developing UAT scripts, executing parallel payroll testing, or supporting system cutovers.
Experience building or improving payroll controls, SOPs, and audit processes.
Experience in a high-growth, global financial services or technology organization.

What We Offer
